title: From Raw Supply to Usable Listings: Normalization and Enrichment
basis: Reconstructed on 2026-11-12 from the published index.md (paragraph for paragraph, in its own order) and spec.md (accepted 2026-10-21), which it replaces. Intent outcome, acceptance criteria AC-1 to AC-3, the thesis and the role are copied unchanged from the normalization-and-enrichment entry in journal-spec.json. Three units were added to the published text: a roadmap paragraph in the introduction (p04), a lead-in to the trade-offs table (p42) and two closing paragraphs before the hand-off (p60, p61).

know: The difference between normalization (a stated value in canonical form, meaning unchanged) and enrichment (facts nobody stated, from registries, models and platform computations), and the ten deterministic normalization steps.
The provenance record and its seven source classes, and the real cost drivers of enrichment at classifieds volume: re-processing, evaluation and human review.
believe: A derived value must never silently overwrite an asserted one, and who wins between seller, feed, registry and model is a product and legal decision per attribute, not an engineering default.
can_do: Specify a provenance record and a per-attribute precedence policy, and design an enrichment pipeline whose steps are idempotent, versioned and replayable.
Decide which enrichers a group shares across brands and which stay in the verticals, and plan a quarter's re-processing budget.

audience.who: Chief and principal architects, data and ML leads, and listing-data owners in classifieds, real-estate and automotive marketplaces.
already_knows: APIs, databases, event streams, search engines and Kubernetes (the book's baseline), data pipelines and the basics of machine learning.
Part II's listing model: the listing aggregate, the canonical category tree, the attribute dictionary and compiled category schemas, the media pipeline and the location model.
Part III so far: the ingestion channels, feed contracts, the partner's run report and the one write path into the listing service.
Veldmark, its brands (Tradeyard, Motorvane, Hearthly, Keybridge), its cast and the fifteen failure-pattern names.
does_not_know: Normalization, enrichment and attribute provenance as this chapter defines them.
VIN decoding, German type-approval codes (HSN/TSN) and licensed vehicle-specification data.
French reference data: DVF transaction data, the DPE energy certificate and the Base Adresse Nationale.
OCR (optical character recognition) as a moderation and enrichment service.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a corrected decoder release, the reader re-runs enrichment without overwriting values dealers fixed by hand, and says what made that possible.
acceptance_criteria.probe: Your VIN-decoder supplier ships corrected data for a popular engine family. Some dealers had fixed the decoded power value by hand on their listings. Using only this chapter: how do you apply the correction, and what must already be in place?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Each value carries provenance (source class, process and version, confidence, time) with the original kept next to the canonical value. The precedence policy in the attribute dictionary says registry values do not overwrite asserted seller or feed values, so dealer-fixed values stay and the new decode is kept as an alternative. The decoder is a versioned, idempotent enricher; the re-run selects affected listings by fingerprint, active listings first, inside a planned re-processing budget, behind an evaluation gate, and writes back to the system of record rather than only to the search index.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reader of the opening alone (the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading) can predict the chapter's sections.
acceptance_criteria.probe: After reading only the callouts and the paragraphs before the first heading: what will this chapter discuss, in what order, and with what kind of evidence?
acceptance_criteria.expected: April 2027 at Veldmark: 23% of bike listings with a frame size, the Essen Golf's 31 decoded attributes and the question of who said each value; normalization versus enrichment, canonical and original values, provenance; ten normalization steps; registry decoding and model-based enrichment; a replayable pipeline with versioned enrichers, human correction and quality scores; the Golf value by value, the bike extraction, the Lyon flat's disclosures and translation; the cost of enrichment; trade-offs, vertical differences, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and questions. Evidence: public company engineering sources, standards and regulation, research, and the fictional Veldmark.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A reverse outline of the chapter, written without the spec, lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the post spec's sections and paragraphs.
Given a model's value that contradicts a legally required disclosure, the reader says what the platform does with each value and why.
acceptance_criteria.probe: An agency lists a flat in France with energy class D. Your image-and-text model predicts class C, and the agency supplied the energy certificate's number. Using only this chapter: what does the platform show, what does it do with the model's value and the certificate, and why?
acceptance_criteria.expected: The platform shows the agency's stated class D: the energy class is a legally required disclosure the advertiser must state, so enrichment verifies it against the energy-certificate register using the certificate number and flags a mismatch back to the agency; it never replaces the value or fills it from a model. The model's value is not shown as the disclosure.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Given a quarter with several schema changes and model releases, the reader names the cost drivers in order of size and the ways to contain them.
acceptance_criteria.probe: This quarter your group plans a category split, a schema change and a new extraction-model version, each touching about 13 million live listings. Using only this chapter: which costs should the plan include, which is likely the largest, and how do you keep them down?
acceptance_criteria.expected: Model calls per backfill are the smallest item (roughly €5,000 per pass over 13.2 million listings in the illustrative model), but each change can need a backfill, so re-processing multiplies them; evaluation of each release on gold samples costs reviewer time (about 33 hours for 2,000 listings); human review of uncertain values is usually the largest variable cost (about 270 reviewer-hours a week). Contain them with prioritized backfills (active listings first), input fingerprints that skip unaffected listings, small or self-hosted models, and a quarterly plan of backfills with compute and review cost.

thesis.question: How do you turn heterogeneous input into consistent, enriched listings?
thesis.claim: Normalization and enrichment are different operations that one pipeline must keep apart in the record: every value is stored in its dictionary's canonical form next to the original as received, with provenance saying who stated or derived it, by which process and version, with what confidence; precedence between seller, feed, registry and model is a per-attribute policy in the attribute dictionary that never lets a derived value silently overwrite an asserted one; and enrichment runs as a versioned, replayable pipeline of idempotent steps that writes back to the listing's system of record, budgeted for re-processing and human review, which cost more than the model calls.
thesis.disputed_by: The common practice of cleaning values in place on import, writing derived values into the same attribute columns as seller statements (or only into the search index), letting the most recent writer win, and budgeting machine-learning enrichment by the price per model call.
thesis.so_what: A Chief Architect who accepts this makes provenance a group standard before the pipelines multiply (Veldmark adopts one vocabulary in October 2027), shares generic enrichers (geocoding, translation, image classification, a model gateway) while keeping VIN decoding and energy-certificate checks in the verticals, puts every enricher including rule tables under model governance, and plans each quarter's backfills with their compute and reviewer cost.
thesis.how_why: Yardstick had no place to store a value the seller had not typed, so extracting the missing frame sizes (23% coverage on bike listings) would have made model output look like seller statements. Motorvane found cars rated against the wrong engine variant because a decoder value had replaced a dealer value, and could not re-run corrected decoding without overwriting dealers' fixes because nothing recorded which value came from where. In the Veldmark cost model, one backfill of Tradeyard's 13.2 million live listings costs roughly €5,000 in model calls, while reviewing uncertain values takes about 270 reviewer-hours a week.

supporting_claims.claim: Normalization (a stated value put in canonical form, meaning unchanged) and enrichment (a fact nobody stated) are different operations with different owners, tests and rules for being overwritten.
Every attribute value is stored in canonical form next to the original as received, with a provenance record of who stated or derived it, by which process and version, with what confidence and when.

Precedence between seller, feed, registry and model is a per-attribute policy in the attribute dictionary that keeps every source's value and never lets a derived value silently overwrite an asserted one; legally required disclosures are verified, never derived.

Enrichment runs as a pipeline of versioned, idempotent steps that writes back to the listing's system of record, releases new versions behind evaluation gates and can be replayed or rolled back value by value.
At classifieds volume, re-processing, evaluation and human review cost more than the model calls, so they are planned and budgeted like migrations.

role.contribution: Turns accepted records into comparable, trustworthy values with recorded origins, which entity resolution matches on and search filters on.

additional_patterns.applies_to: scene to architecture: the two Veldmark failures first, then the vocabulary, operations and pipeline that resolve them
in-practice to questions: worked cases, then cost, then the decisions a group faces

flow.rationale: The chapter follows the book's chapter shape and each section supplies what the next needs. The scene comes first so the reader holds the two failures (a model value with nowhere to live, a decoder value that overwrote a dealer's) that every later rule answers. The concepts section defines normalization, enrichment, canonical and original values and provenance before the normalization steps and enrichers use those words. Normalization comes before enrichment because enrichers read normalized values. The architecture follows both, because its rules (write-back, idempotency keys, precedence, release gates) govern the steps just described. The worked cases then apply the rules to the Golf, the bikes, the Lyon flat and Tradeyard Belgium, and the cost section prices the pipeline only once the reader has seen what re-processing and review are. Trade-offs, vertical differences, failure modes, the Chief Architect's view and the questions draw on all of it. Moving the architecture before the concepts would use provenance and precedence before they are defined; moving the cost before the cases would quote backfill and review figures for a pipeline the reader has not yet seen run.

sections.heading: Concepts: Canonical Values, Derived Facts and Their Origins
sections.controlling_idea: Normalization and enrichment are different operations, each value is kept in canonical and original form, and a provenance record with a closed set of source classes says where each value came from.

advances_thesis.how: Defines the distinction and the record the thesis depends on.

transition_in.carries_over: Ingrid's question about who said each value.
transition_in.introduces: The vocabulary needed to answer it.

flow.rationale: The distinction first, then the two stored forms of a value, then the provenance record's fields, then its source classes, then one filled-in record (the Golf's power) written in that vocabulary, then where the record lives. Each step uses the terms defined before it.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Normalization and enrichment have different owners, tests and rules for being overwritten, because a normalized value is still the seller's statement and an enriched one is the platform's assertion.

evidence.what: Normalization versus enrichment: what it does, example ('48.000 km' to 48,000 km; VIN to body type HATCHBACK), whether meaning changes, determinism, provenance, failure mode.
evidence.shows: The two operations differ on every property that governs overwriting and testing.

evidence.what: Figure 1: a seller's value translated into a canonical tag beside a registry lookup that adds tags nobody typed.
evidence.shows: Shows the meaning-preserving and meaning-adding operations side by side.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Each attribute value is stored twice, as a canonical value for every system that compares or computes and as the original value with unit and locale for display, audit and re-normalization.

evidence.what: Schema.org QuantitativeValue with UN/CEFACT unit codes KMT and SMI; Google Merchant Center prices as a number plus an ISO 4217 code.
evidence.source: schema.org Vehicle, V30.1, 2026; Google Merchant Center, n.d.
evidence.shows: Standard codes exist for the canonical form, so the dictionary need not invent its own.

transition_in.carries_over: A normalized value that is still the seller's statement.
transition_in.introduces: The two forms in which every value is kept.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Provenance is a small record attached to every attribute value, naming its source class, the party that asserted it, the process and version, confidence, alternatives, status and time.

transition_in.introduces: The record that says where each came from.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Provenance uses seven source classes that should be a closed vocabulary across the group, each with its own default trust.

evidence.what: seller, partner_feed, registry, catalog, model, moderator, platform, with meaning, typical examples and default trust.
evidence.shows: Gives the reader the vocabulary a precedence policy is written in.

transition_in.introduces: The closed set of source classes it may take.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The Golf's power shows why the record needs more than a source: the decoder returned two candidates, the dealer's value matched one, and the record keeps the dealer's value with both registry candidates as alternatives.

evidence.what: The Golf's power: the VIN decoder returned two candidates, 96 and 110 kW (two derivatives of the model), and the dealer's 96 kW matches one, so the conflict is resolved; then the record of vehicle.power_kw: canonical 96, original '96 kW' (de-DE), source partner_feed via TSP-031, asserted by the seller, normalizer units@2027.03, registry alternatives 96 and 110 from licensed-vin@2027.04, with one pointer forward to the registry section.
evidence.source: Veldmark illustration
evidence.shows: Shows the record, in the source-class vocabulary just defined, holding the asserted value and the derived alternatives.

transition_in.carries_over: The record's fields and the source classes.
transition_in.introduces: One filled-in record, the Golf's power.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The listing aggregate holds the values with provenance and the attribute dictionary says per attribute which sources are allowed and how conflicts resolve, while this chapter's pipeline produces the records.

transition_in.carries_over: The provenance record, its source classes and the Golf's example.
transition_in.introduces: Where the record lives and who sets the precedence rules.

sections.heading: Normalization: Ten Deterministic Steps
sections.controlling_idea: A multi-country listing platform needs ten small, deterministic normalization steps, each versioned, flagging rather than guessing, with owned mapping tables.

advances_thesis.how: Shows normalization as meaning-preserving, deterministic and replayable, with the original kept.

transition_in.carries_over: Normalization as defined in the concepts.
transition_in.introduces: The concrete steps it consists of.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: In my judgement any listing platform operating in several European countries needs the same ten normalization steps, each with a failure it prevents and a rule.

evidence.what: Encoding, text, numbers and locale, units, enumerations, named entities, dates and times, prices and currency, addresses, phone numbers and contact data, with what goes wrong and the rule.
evidence.shows: Each step is a small deterministic rule, so the whole can be versioned and replayed.

evidence.what: Vinted: about 2,000,000 unique brand values restricted to about 40,000 verified brands, cutting P99 facet latency by about 15 ms.
evidence.source: Vinted Engineering, 2023
evidence.shows: Entity normalization against a verified dictionary pays off in search.

evidence.what: mobile.de: ISO 8601 date-times in the Europe/Berlin offset and yyyyMM first registration; libpostal 99.45% full-parse accuracy, 60+ languages, about 1.8 GB model; Base Adresse Nationale under Etalab 2.0.
evidence.source: mobile.de Seller-API, n.d.; libpostal, n.d.; adresse.data.gouv.fr, n.d.
evidence.shows: Real formats and tools behind the date and address rules.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Three design rules apply to every step: normalizers are versioned code with test suites, failure to normalize is a flag rather than a guess, and mapping tables are data with owners.

transition_in.introduces: The rules that apply across all of them.

sections.heading: Enrichment: Facts Nobody Typed
sections.controlling_idea: Enrichment adds facts nobody typed, from registries where they exist and from models otherwise, and the public evidence says models should propose values against a schema passed in, be validated and be released behind measured gates.

advances_thesis.how: Shows enrichment as meaning-adding and versioned, and gathers the evidence for gated, schema-driven model enrichment.

transition_in.introduces: Enrichment, which adds facts.

flow.rationale: The four jobs and the list of enrichers first, then registries (vehicles, then what they teach, then real estate), then models. Registries come before models because where the truth exists elsewhere, decoding beats extraction.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Enrichment adds facts sellers cannot know, fills attributes sellers did not provide, adds platform-computed signals and prepares the listing for other languages and systems.

evidence.what: Ten enrichments grouped by the four jobs in a Job column (facts sellers cannot know: registry decoding, geocoding, property and regulatory data; attributes sellers did not provide: category prediction, text and image extraction; platform-computed signals: market value, quality scores; other languages and systems: translation, embeddings), with inputs, outputs, source class and owner.
evidence.shows: Each enrichment has a source class and an owner, which the pipeline and precedence policy rely on.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Where a registry exists, decoding beats extraction from text, and vehicle marketplaces decode VINs and type-approval codes against public or licensed specification data.

evidence.what: NHTSA vPIC: batches of up to 50 VINs, partial VINs with '*', downloadable databases; mobile.de Seller-API: hsn, tsn and schwackeCode from Eurotax/Schwacke; Autotrader UK: taxonomy to derivative, valuations keyed on derivative ID, first registration and mileage.
evidence.source: NHTSA vPIC API, n.d.; mobile.de Seller-API manual, n.d.; Autotrader developer portal, n.d.
evidence.shows: Authoritative specification data exists for vehicles and is used by real marketplaces.

transition_in.carries_over: Registry decoding, the first enrichment in the table.
transition_in.introduces: Vehicle registries and decoders.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Decoders return families of candidates as well as exact answers and change with the supplier's releases, so each decoded value must record its decoder and data version.

transition_in.introduces: The two lessons decoders teach the pipeline.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Real estate has registries too, but authoritative does not mean clean, so provenance must say which register and extract a value came from.

evidence.what: DVF transaction register, last five years, updated in April and October; ADEME DPE dataset of existing dwellings since July 2021, updated weekly, about 15.8 million records as of October 2026, raw diagnostician input ADEME does not correct.
evidence.source: data.gouv.fr, last updated 2026; ADEME open data, 2026
evidence.shows: Even official registers carry uncorrected data, so the source must be recorded.

transition_in.introduces: Property registries and their limits.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The public evidence on model-based enrichment points one way: propose values against a schema passed in, validate the output, gate releases on measured precision, and keep the big model offline and the small model online; two further cases bear on the pipeline, linked to rules 3 and 4 of the architecture.

evidence.what: Mercari title suggestions (2023), dynamic attributes with a fine-tuned 2B model (2024) and re-categorization estimated at USD 1 million and 1.9 years (2024); Etsy's reported 31% to 91% coverage via a third-party summary (2025); Adevinta OCR at 330 million requests a month (2023); mobile.de price rating recalculated when images arrive (n.d.); Google Merchant Center's automatic categories (n.d.).
evidence.source: Mercari Engineering 2023, 2024; ZenML LLMOps Database 2025; Adevinta Tech Blog 2023; mobile.de n.d.; Google Merchant Center n.d.
evidence.shows: Each case shows one part of the pattern and says which: schema at request time, validation, gates, cost of brute force, a specialized model online beating a general external API (Adevinta), dependency between enrichers, receivers classifying for themselves.

transition_in.carries_over: Registries, where the truth exists elsewhere.
transition_in.introduces: Models, used where it does not.

sections.heading: Architecture: A Replayable Pipeline That Writes Back
sections.controlling_idea: Enrichment runs as a loop around the listing service whose rules (write-back, idempotency keys, declared dependencies, no silent overwrites, a small blocking set) make it replayable, with versioned releases, human correction loops and quality scores around it.

advances_thesis.how: Specifies the pipeline the thesis calls for and the precedence rule it enforces.

transition_in.carries_over: Many enrichers, registry and model, each with its own version.
transition_in.introduces: The pipeline that runs them safely.

flow.rationale: The five rules first, because releases, correction loops and quality scores all assume write-back and per-value provenance. Releases follow the rules they extend to re-processing; correction loops supply the labels the release gate needs; quality scores come last because they summarize what releases and corrections leave on each listing, including how much of it people confirmed.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Enrichers write back to the listing's system of record through an ApplyEnrichment command checked against the listing version, and never only into the search index.

evidence.what: Figure 2, after rule 1: the enrichment pipeline as a loop around the listing service, read models rebuilt from the listing, suggestions to sellers becoming labels.
evidence.shows: Shows that enrichment results enter the listing like any other write.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Each enrichment step is a pure function with an idempotency key built from listing ID, input fingerprint, enricher ID and version and reference-data version, so it re-runs only when its inputs change.

transition_in.introduces: Rule 2.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Enrichers declare dependencies, and the orchestrator re-runs the affected subgraph when an input changes.

transition_in.carries_over: Steps that re-run when their inputs change.
transition_in.introduces: The order between steps.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Derived values never silently overwrite asserted ones: the dictionary's precedence policy decides what is used, the listing keeps every source's value, and a retired suggestion remains as a training label.

transition_in.introduces: The rule about whose value wins.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Some steps block publication but most do not, and each has a degraded mode.

evidence.what: Normalization of required attributes, category, vehicle decode, geocoding (blocking or usually blocking); extraction, translation, embeddings, quality score, price rating (not blocking), with why and degraded mode.
evidence.shows: Only values that drive validation, privacy or fees must exist before publication.

transition_in.carries_over: Rules about how steps run and write.
transition_in.introduces: When they must finish.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The blocking set must fit the publication budget, so a synchronous language-model call on the insertion path is costly.

evidence.what: Tradeyard's publication target of 90 seconds at p95, owned by the publication-pipeline chapter.
evidence.source: scenario-ledger.md
evidence.shows: The budget limits what can block.

transition_in.introduces: The time budget they must fit.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: An enricher changes when its code, its reference data or the schema it fills changes, and each change raises the question of which existing listings to re-process, in what order and with what protection.

evidence.what: Figure 3: releasing an enricher like a schema migration: shadow test against labels, prioritized backfill through the same write path, churn monitoring, value-level rollback.
evidence.shows: Shows the release process that answers the question.

transition_in.introduces: What happens when one of its enrichers changes.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The release gate works when value churn is measured against the evaluation's prediction and rollback is a data operation made possible by per-value versions.

evidence.what: Etsy's reported practice of halting production runs when precision or recall drifts from a baseline.
evidence.source: ZenML LLMOps Database summary of Etsy Code as Craft, 2025
evidence.shows: A public precedent for the gate.

evidence.what: A new version changing 4% of values where evaluation predicted 1%.
evidence.shows: Churn reveals a difference between the sample and production.

transition_in.introduces: The two details that make its gate work.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Every human decision about a value is a label, and the pipeline should collect them deliberately from sellers, moderators, buyers and professionals.

evidence.what: Kleinanzeigen's photo-based assistant lets sellers accept suggestions fully, partially or not at all.
evidence.source: mobiFlip, 2025
evidence.shows: Seller choices on suggestions are a real, recordable label source.

transition_in.carries_over: The release gate, which needs labels.
transition_in.introduces: Where labels come from: every human decision about a value.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Label quality is the hidden risk, and a small, regularly refreshed gold sample labeled by trained reviewers calibrates the rest.

transition_in.introduces: Why they are noisy and what calibrates them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: In my judgement a listing quality score should be built from four measurable dimensions defined per category schema: completeness, validity, consistency and confidence.

sections.heading: In Practice: The Essen Golf and Three Other Cases
sections.controlling_idea: Four Veldmark cases show the rules at work: provenance resolves the Golf's power conflict, model provenance lets the bike extraction fill values safely, legally required disclosures are verified rather than derived, and translation is enrichment like any other.

advances_thesis.how: Applies provenance, precedence and the pipeline to four concrete listings.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Following the Golf's values from the DMS feed to the listing shows which were normalized from the dealer's statement and which were added by decoding and valuation.

evidence.what: Make, model, engine and trim, power, first registration, mileage, price, color, equipment, 26 further decoded values (31 in all), location and market value (€22,800, 'good price', re-run on 22 April at €21,400), with raw value, canonical value, source class and action.
evidence.source: scenario-ledger.md, Essen Golf; ledger listing-ingestion line on feed timing

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Enrichment raised the Golf from 9 to 23 of 26 recommended attributes and put it into the body-type, transmission and fuel filters most buyers use.

evidence.what: 14 of 14 required and 9 of 26 recommended attributes before; 23 of 26 after.
evidence.source: scenario-ledger.md, Essen Golf enrichment
evidence.shows: Completeness determines whether filtering buyers see the listing.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The power value shows the failure provenance prevents: with both decoder candidates stored and a policy that the consistent dealer value wins, the rating reads the right derivative and a later decode updates only cars without a dealer value.

evidence.what: Figure 4: the Golf with source tags; the dealer's 96 kW resolves the conflict between candidates 96 and 110 kW, with the other kept.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Tradeyard's bike-extraction pilot followed the public pattern: a self-hosted small model given the schema keys at request time, validation against the schema, suggestions for new listings and model provenance for live ones, gated on a gold sample.

transition_in.introduces: Its results.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Enrichment normalized the Lyon flat's three addresses and assigned its area, but verified rather than derived its energy class, because the class is a disclosure the advertiser must state.

sections.heading: The Cost of Enrichment at Scale
sections.controlling_idea: At classifieds volume, model calls are the smallest cost of enrichment; re-processing multiplies cost and people (evaluation and review) are the main cost.

advances_thesis.how: Prices the pipeline and shows where the cost lies.

transition_in.carries_over: The four cases, scaled up to the whole stock.
transition_in.introduces: What it costs.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A rough Veldmark cost model, with illustrative prices, shows that the price of the model calls themselves (calls times price per call) is usually the smallest number on the enrichment bill.

evidence.what: Text extraction on 2.3M new listings and about 0.9M edits a week (about €1,300 a week); one backfill of 13.2M listings (about €5,000 per pass); evaluation per release (about 33 reviewer-hours for 2,000 listings); human review of 1% of 3.2M weekly runs (about 270 reviewer-hours a week); image enrichment within about €3.1M a year.
evidence.source: Veldmark illustration; scenario-ledger.md live listings and ml-platform lines
evidence.shows: Model cost per pass is small next to recurring review and evaluation.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Three conclusions follow: per-call model cost is rarely the constraint, re-processing is the multiplier, and people are the main cost.

evidence.what: Mercari's USD 1 million estimate for brute-forcing a large API model over more than 3 billion items, answered with a cheaper architecture.
evidence.source: Mercari Engineering, 2024
evidence.shows: Model cost is an architecture choice, not a fixed constraint.

transition_in.introduces: What it means for planning.

sections.heading: Failure Modes
sections.controlling_idea: Eight failure modes follow from breaking the chapter's rules, each with the rule that prevents it.

advances_thesis.how: Shows what happens when each part of the thesis is missing.

transition_in.introduces: What goes wrong without them.

flow.rationale: A lead paragraph names the eight failures as what happens when the rules are broken. Then provenance failures first (mixed values, re-runs over corrections, index-only values), then normalization failures (misparses), then model, mapping and disclosure failures, then cost. Each is one paragraph led by its bold name.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The design works only while its rules are kept; without them enrichment fails in eight recurring ways, each with the rule that prevents it.
Once derived values are indistinguishable from asserted ones they cannot be separated, and every later decision is made blind.

transition_in.introduces: The first, mixed derived and asserted values.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A new decoder or model version that writes every value it computes overwrites the corrections of sellers and moderators unless precedence and per-value provenance stop it.

transition_in.introduces: What a re-run does to them.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Enrichment written only into the index vanishes at the next reindex and cannot be shown or audited.

transition_in.introduces: Values lost to a reindex.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Silent misparses, such as 48,000 km read as 48 km, need a plausibility check from the dictionary on every numeric normalizer.

transition_in.introduces: A normalization failure.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: An extraction model released without a labeled sample, threshold and churn monitoring writes its error rate into millions of listings.

transition_in.introduces: A model failure.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Alias tables that force unknown values into the nearest known one turn a mapping gap into wrong data.

transition_in.introduces: Ungoverned mapping tables.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: A platform that corrects or fills a legally required disclosure publishes a statement the advertiser did not make.

transition_in.introduces: Wrong data in a legal disclosure.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Several full backfills in one quarter can exhaust its inference and review budget unless backfills are planned like migrations.

transition_in.introduces: A failure of budget.

sections.heading: The Chief Architect's View
sections.controlling_idea: A Chief Architect makes provenance a group standard, shares generic enrichers while keeping domain ones local, governs every enricher, puts precedence in the dictionary, budgets re-processing and measures enrichment by liquidity.

advances_thesis.how: Turns each supporting claim into a group decision.

transition_in.introduces: The decisions that prevent them at group level.

flow.rationale: A lead paragraph says the failures are prevented by group decisions. Then provenance first because every other decision depends on it; then the share line, governance and precedence; then budget and measurement; then what to watch.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The failures are prevented more reliably by decisions taken once for the whole group than by each team's care, and six such decisions follow.
Make provenance a group standard before the pipelines multiply, as Veldmark did in October 2027.

evidence.what: One provenance vocabulary (seven source classes plus process, version, confidence and time) adopted in October 2027 with the taxonomy and attribute service.
evidence.source: scenario-ledger.md, group provenance vocabulary
evidence.shows: A standard set early avoids retrofitting four listing stores.

transition_in.introduces: The first, provenance as a group standard.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Share generic enrichers and keep domain enrichers in the verticals, the same line as for ingestion.

transition_in.introduces: Which enrichers the group shares.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Put every enricher, rule tables included, under model governance with an owner, version, evaluation set, gate and dashboard.

transition_in.introduces: How each is governed.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Decide precedence per attribute in the attribute dictionary, as a product and legal decision the pipeline enforces.

transition_in.introduces: The policy over their outputs.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Budget re-processing explicitly each quarter, because an unplanned backfill waits for capacity.

evidence.what: The bikes split was planned with its backfill; the Motorvane decoder correction was not and waited three months.
evidence.source: Veldmark illustration
evidence.shows: Planning decides whether a correction ships.

transition_in.introduces: Budget.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Treat enrichment as a supply-side liquidity lever and measure it by filtered-search coverage and contact rates.

transition_in.introduces: Value.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: The numbers to watch are coverage, model-only share, gold-sample precision, value churn, suggestion rejection, disputes and the unknown-value queues.

transition_in.introduces: The measures that show whether they hold.

sections.heading: Questions to Ask
sections.controlling_idea: Ten review questions test whether a marketplace's pipeline records provenance, keeps originals, writes back, enforces precedence, fits the publication budget, re-processes safely, protects disclosures, collects labels, budgets backfills and draws the share line by meaning.

advances_thesis.how: Turns the thesis into checks a reader can run.

transition_in.introduces: Questions that test them in a review.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ten questions test a pipeline against the chapter's rules, from provenance for any value to how the share line between brands is drawn.

conclusion.heading: From Clean Records to Duplicates
conclusion.synthesis: Keeping the original, recording provenance and deciding precedence per attribute only work together: the original makes normalization replayable, provenance makes precedence enforceable, and precedence makes re-running enrichment safe. Remove any one and a part fails: without the original a corrected normalizer cannot be re-run, without provenance the policy cannot tell a dealer's fix from a decode, and without the policy the Golf's decoder correction tramples dealers' fixes.
conclusion.so_what: The order of work for a group is the vocabulary and the policy first, before the enrichers multiply, then re-processing and review planned as a recurring budget line rather than a one-off project.

callback.to: Ingrid Halvorsen's question in the scene: for each value, do we know who said it, what we did to it and whether we may change it?
callback.how: The Golf, the bikes and the Lyon flat now answer yes, value by value.

takeaway.content: Fix the provenance vocabulary and the precedence policy before adding enrichers, and plan each quarter's backfills with their review cost.

hand_off.carries_over: The canonical addresses, decoded VINs and image hashes that normalization and enrichment produce.
hand_off.introduces: The problem those comparable values expose, that several listings describe the same flat or car, and the capability that decides when listings are one thing and what each audience sees.

paragraphs.controlling_idea: Ingrid's question now has the answer yes: every value on the Golf, the bikes and the Lyon flat says who stated or derived it, by which process and version, and whether it may change.

The original value, provenance and per-attribute precedence work only together, so a group fixes the vocabulary and the policy before its enrichers multiply and budgets re-processing and review as a recurring cost.
